stages.label: Supplies
stages.text: Receive, sort and store everything the cargo ships bring.

stages.label: Power & comms
stages.text: Keep the lights on and the radio clear.

stages.label: Robotics
stages.text: Let rovers and arms work outside, safely and on their own.

stages.label: Habitat & build
stages.text: Shape decks, modules and parts that last for years.

stages.label: Safety
stages.text: Prove every system works, every day and every night.

stages.label: Mission
stages.text: Reach the goals the station was built for.

roles.name: Crew Coach
roles.summary: The Crew Coach helps the crew work well together by guiding routines, easing friction and keeping everyone learning.
roles.quote: I help the crew stay in sync by clearing blockers, running good routines and making room for every voice on board.
tasks: Run the daily crew briefing and the weekly review
Coach teams in shared routines and clear handovers
Remove blockers and keep improving how the crew works
Keep communication open between shifts and modules
competence: Knows how small teams work best under pressure
Supports crew performance and steady improvement
Encourages sharing knowledge across every module

roles.name: Flight Software Engineer – Autopilot
roles.summary: The Flight Software Engineer writes the autopilot code that keeps shuttles and rovers on course.
roles.quote: I teach our vehicles to steer themselves with lean, reliable code that runs on tiny onboard computers.
tasks: Write autopilot software for shuttles and rovers
Tune control loops for small onboard computers
Bring trained models into the flight software
Measure timing, memory and power on the real vehicle
competence: Strong programming skills for small onboard computers
Knowledge of control systems and machine learning
Understanding of limits like memory, timing and power
Works across software, robotics and flight topics

roles.name: Research Lead
roles.summary: The Research Lead turns open questions into experiments and new ideas into the station's next upgrades.
roles.quote: I solve the hard questions on board by combining curiosity, careful experiments and a good look at tomorrow.
tasks: Plan experiments and the methods behind them
Break complex problems into testable steps
Turn promising results into station upgrades
Share findings with every crew and module
competence: Deep expertise in science and engineering methods
Knowledge of experiment design and data analysis
Analytical problem solving and system thinking
Explains complex ideas in plain words

roles.name: Greenhouse Lead
roles.summary: The Greenhouse Lead grows the station's food, from the first seedling to a steady harvest line.
roles.quote: I connect plants, light and water into a garden that feeds the whole crew, season after season.
tasks: Plan crops, light cycles and nutrient mixes
Turn test beds into a steady harvest line
Balance water, power and space with other modules
Review yields and share what grows best
competence: Deep knowledge of plants in closed habitats
Understanding of light, water and air systems
Systems thinking across food, power and waste
Leadership, planning and clear communication

roles.name: Water Recycler
roles.summary: The Water Recycler keeps every drop moving: collected, filtered, stored and clean enough to drink.
roles.quote: I turn used water into fresh water by watching every filter, every tank and every sample.
tasks: Run collection, filtering and storage loops
Test water samples every shift
Automate the checks on pumps and filters
Report water quality and fix leaks fast
competence: Knowledge of filtration and recycling loops
Experience with pumps, sensors and simple scripts
Understanding of water chemistry on board
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills

roles.name: Power Engineer
roles.summary: The Power Engineer balances solar panels, batteries and loads so the station never goes dark.
roles.quote: I keep every module powered by trimming the load and squeezing the most out of every panel.
tasks: Manage solar panels, batteries and power lines
Trim loads and plan power for every shift
Install and test new power hardware
Find and fix faults before they spread
competence: Expertise in electrical systems and batteries
Knowledge of solar power and load planning
Understanding of switches, converters and controllers
Calm troubleshooting under pressure

roles.name: Radio Operator
roles.summary: The Radio Operator keeps contact with ground control and passing ships, clear through any static.
roles.quote: I make sure every message gets through by turning faint, noisy static into a clear voice.
tasks: Run the daily contact windows with ground control
Clean up noisy transmissions and log every call
Maintain antennas, receivers and backup links
Relay messages between crews and visiting ships
competence: Expertise in radio systems and antennas
Strong ear for weak and noisy transmissions
Knowledge of filters and transmission protocols
Clear, calm and precise communication

roles.name: Rover Robotics Engineer
roles.summary: The Rover Robotics Engineer builds and teaches the rovers that work outside the hull.
roles.quote: I put a brain in our rovers so they can drill, carry and explore while the crew stays safe inside.
tasks: Build and repair rovers and robotic arms
Train rovers to recognise rocks, tools and hazards
Test new behaviours on the practice field
Work with power, flight and safety teams
competence: Expertise in robotics and onboard computing
Knowledge of sensors, motors and machine learning
Understanding of limits in power and weight
Strong hands-on and problem-solving skills

roles.name: Station Architect
roles.summary: The Station Architect draws how modules, docks and trusses fit together into one safe station.
roles.quote: I draw the blueprint of the station, every bolt and every beam, so it can grow without breaking.
tasks: Define how modules, docks and trusses connect
Turn mission needs into a buildable layout
Balance mass, air and power across the station
Guide build crews on interfaces and trade-offs
competence: Strong expertise in structures and layouts
Knowledge of docking, mass and power budgets
Understanding of how modules share air and power
Guides decisions across every build crew

roles.name: Mission Commander
roles.summary: The Mission Commander sets the course, picks the priorities and keeps every crew aimed at the same goal.
roles.quote: I turn the mission into clear priorities, so every crew knows what matters today and why.
tasks: Set and order the mission goals for each week
Align ground control wishes with what the crew can do
Lead planning and the big decisions on board
Make sure every shift adds real value to the mission
competence: Strong sense for priorities and trade-offs
Balances crew, mission and technical needs
Clear communication with ground and crew
Strategic thinking and calm decisions

roles.name: Habitat Designer
roles.summary: The Habitat Designer builds the decks, cabins and gardens where the crew lives and works.
roles.quote: I design living spaces that hold the weight of daily life and still feel like home.
tasks: Lay out decks, cabins and shared spaces
Turn crew needs into practical designs
Guide choices on materials and space
Work with build crews on every refit
competence: Strong expertise in habitat and interior design
Understanding of life support, light and noise
Balances cosiness, safety and weight- Strong communication across all crews

roles.name: Life-Support Manager
roles.summary: The Life-Support Manager keeps oxygen, water, heat and pressure running for everyone on board.
roles.quote: I keep the backbone of the station strong, so nobody has to think about the air they breathe.
tasks: Manage oxygen, water, heat and pressure systems
Plan maintenance and spare parts for every loop
Coordinate repairs with power and water crews
Keep every life-support system available and safe
competence: Knowledge of air, water and thermal systems
Understanding of alarms, backups and redundancy
Experience with maintenance and operations
Strong coordination and planning skills

roles.name: Safety Officer
roles.summary: The Safety Officer owns the drills, checklists and standards that keep the station safe.
roles.quote: I design how we prove the station is safe, from the spacesuit up to the whole station.
tasks: Define drills, checklists and safety standards
Plan checks for suits, modules and the whole station
Coach crews in emergency routines
Keep improving how fast and well we check
competence: Expertise in safety engineering and risk
Knowledge of drills, checklists and standards
Understanding of every station system
Strong coaching and communication skills

roles.name: Night Inspector
roles.summary: The Night Inspector walks the station every night and catches small problems before they grow.
roles.quote: I keep the station healthy by checking every hatch, valve and gauge while the others sleep.
tasks: Run the nightly inspection round
Log readings from every module and gauge
Report leaks, faults and wear in the morning briefing
Improve the checklists after every finding
competence: Experience with inspections and measurements
Knowledge of station systems and gauges
Understanding of maintenance routines
Sharp eye for small changes

roles.name: Station Machinist
roles.summary: The Station Machinist makes and repairs the parts and tools the station runs on.
roles.quote: I forge the parts that power us all, from a tiny bracket to a brand-new pump housing.
tasks: Make and repair parts in the station workshop
Print spare parts instead of waiting for cargo
Fit new tools into existing modules
Ask crews what they need and build it
competence: Strong machining and repair skills
Knowledge of 3D printing and materials
Understanding of how station systems fit together
Builds parts that are easy to service
